label: copy-phase input h fed back as the 1st or 2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is h at recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the fed-back h is original token 0 (step right after <DEL>) or original token 1. Magnitude is set by position: strong (~0.8-1.0 of max, ~82% of mass) when h was the first original token and comes in right after <DEL>; weak (~0.05-0.25 of max) when h was the second original token. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, never on h later in the copy (recall_idx >= 3), and almost never on any other token. False positives are mostly short sequences (L=3) where h is the second original token.

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split I get precision 0.981, recall 0.9997 and mass recall 1.0. The dev profile shows all activation in the copy phase, at recall_idx 1 (82.4% of mass) and 2 (17.6%), and 32845 of 32854 active steps have in_tok h.

There is one systematic false-positive class. With L=3, an h at recall_idx 2 almost never fires: the predicate (recall_idx==2)&(L==3) has test precision 0.05 over 436 predicted steps, which is about 414 of the 635 test false positives. With L=4 its precision is 0.91. The explanation does report this ('most false positives are short sequences (seen with L=3)'), but the label leaves it out.

At recall_idx 2 the activation is small and grows with length: about 0.03 to 0.12 at L=4 or 5 and about 0.20 to 0.24 at L=7 to 9. At recall_idx 1 it is about 0.8 to 0.9. This matches the stated ranges.

The 11 missed test steps carry about 0% of the mass. They are tiny activations of 0.01 to 0.06 on h at recall_idx 3 when h was also the first original token, or on r, 3 or g at recall_idx 1. This is scattered noise.
